post.caption: Fort Knox's gold arrived by mail. The vault was finished in December 1936. The first gold arrived in January 1937, from New York and Philadelphia. It traveled as registered mail, run by the Post Office. Postal inspectors planned the guard, with decoy trains and machine guns. Each crate held 16 gold bars and weighed about 500 pounds. A single bar weighs about 27.5 pounds. In 1941, a bigger move took 45 trains and 337 cars. No one person knows all the steps to open the vault. It sits about 30 miles southwest of Louisville, Kentucky.
